_status: VERIFIED -- aluminium, glass, brick_clay, timber, and now structural_steel are all ifc_primary_source tier (see each entry's source field); structural_steel is confirmed correct at 2.5 kgCO2e/kg (IFC India Table 14, p.69 -- prior citation of p.67 was wrong) and is now CEA-adjustment-ready with a derived energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp of 0.76, same method used for rebar. aluminium, glass, and brick_clay also now carry energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp, derived the same way from IFC India Table 16 (Annex C), so all four IFC-primary-source materials in this file can now go through the same CEA grid adjustment concrete/rebar already get -- that wiring itself is not yet done, see cea_adjustment.py. aac_block, cement_plaster, ceramic_tile, and paint remain PLACEHOLDER, unchanged. timber remains ICE v4.1-sourced (not IFC), and is NOT CEA-adjustable under the current method -- see timber entry's note.
_note: Concrete (rcc/pcc) and reinforcement steel are NOT in this file -- those are read from the existing ice_db_factors.json (ifc_india section, real Indian production data, CEA-adjusted) via app.services.ice_factors, so Phase 1 and Phase 2 share one factor source for those two materials rather than risking two numbers drifting apart. The categories in THIS file are the ones ice_db_factors.json does not cover at all yet.

structural_steel.source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017) Table 14, Annex A, p.69 -- 'Steel section' = 2.5 kgCO2e/kg, cradle-to-gate A1-A3, IPCC AR5 (corrected from a prior p.67 citation -- p.67 is the aluminium/brick section of the same table, not steel). Same India-specific source and methodology as reinforcement steel. energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp (0.76) derived from Table 16, Annex C, p.78: Electricity (0.50) + Fuels (1.40) of the 2.5 kgCO2e/kg total, same derivation method used for ifc_india.steel_rebar's 0.7538 (verified by reproducing that figure from rebar's own Table 16 row: (0.46+1.50)/2.6 = 0.7538, exact match). Not yet wired through ice_factors.py/ice_db_factors.json's structured lookup -- duplicated here for now, same as before.

brick_clay.source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017), Table 14 / Annex A, p.67-68. Cradle-to-gate A1-A3, IPCC AR5. Brick assumptions stakeholder-validated in Annex E by Godavari Power & Ispat and Godrej Construction. Default value (0.39) is the blended common/facing brick average; by_kiln_type breakdown available if the BOQ or classifier can identify kiln type. energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp (0.9231) derived from Table 16, Annex C, p.76: Electricity (0) + Fuels (0.36) of the 0.39 kgCO2e/kg total for 'Brick (common/facing)' -- applies to the default blended figure only; by-kiln-type fractions were not separately derived. Corroborating but NOT used as primary: Jay Jalaram Brick Works EPD (EPD-IES-0014544, Godhra, Gujarat, India, published 2024-07-29, third-party verified, International EPD System) declares 0.0805 kgCO2e/kg for their Bull's trench kiln bricks -- about 4x lower than IFC's Bull's trench figure for the same kiln type, likely due to a more efficient/biomass-heavy actual fuel mix than IFC's generic 2017 assumption (85% hard coal / 15% biomass). Logged here rather than substituted in, pending further investigation.

aluminium.source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017), Table 14 / Annex A, p.67. Cradle-to-gate A1-A3, IPCC AR5. Stakeholder-validated in Annex E by Hindalco Industries' CTO, Dr. Pradip Banerjee, who confirmed ~97% of India's large-scale smelters run on captive coal power -- the reason this figure is far higher than global-average aluminium factors (ICE v4.1's European-mix figure is ~6.6-8.1 kgCO2e/kg, not applicable to India's coal-heavy grid). Cross-checked against three other India-specific sources, all of which independently confirm aluminium is far higher than the previous 8.1 placeholder: Hindalco's own disclosed FY2016-20 operational GHG intensity (~19.8-20.6 tCO2e/tonne, corporate Scope 1+2, narrower boundary than a full LCA); NITI Aayog's January 2026 Aluminium Sector Decarbonisation roadmap (national average 20-21 tCO2/t, global average 15 tCO2/t); Global Efficiency Intelligence's 'Aluminum Climate Impact 2025' report (India 2023 data, 16.3 tonnes CO2/tonne primary, electrolysis+refining+PFC+anode only, excludes downstream). IFC's 31 was kept as primary for methodological consistency -- it's the only one of the four that's a full cradle-to-gate LCA on the same basis as every other verified factor in this catalog, rather than a narrower corporate-disclosure or process-only boundary. Default value uses the 'ingot' figure; by_product_form breakdown available if the BOQ or classifier can identify the specific product (window frame, cladding, sheet, etc.) -- window-frame extrusion (26) is meaningfully lower than profiled cladding (35), so using the single default may over- or under-state depending on what's actually being installed. energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp (0.8968) derived from Table 16, Annex C, p.75: Electricity (25) + Fuels (2.8) of the 31 kgCO2e/kg total, for the 'ingot' row specifically -- the by-product-form breakdown does not have separately-derived fractions, only the default 'ingot' figure does.

glass.source: IFC India Construction Materials Database (2017), Table 14 / Annex A, p.68 -- float glass, 1.2 kgCO2e/kg, cradle-to-gate A1-A3. Corroborated by Asahi India Glass (AIS) EPD of Processed Glass (EPD registration S-P-01411 / EPD-IES-0001411, Taloja plant, India, cradle-to-gate A1-A3, third-party verified by Metsims Sustainability Consulting, LCA by Thinkstep -- the same firm behind the IFC India database). The AIS EPD's own Table 13 attributes ~46% of its Heat Tempered Glass GWP (44.7 kgCO2e/m^2 at 6mm) to float glass production, backing out to roughly 1.4 kgCO2e/kg for the float-glass component alone -- consistent with IFC's 1.2. processed_glass_kgco2e_per_m2_6mm gives the AIS EPD's per-m^2 figures for finished products (tempered/laminated/IGU/printed) -- more representative of an actual glazing BOQ line than raw float glass, and areal-based rather than per-kg. NOTE: the AIS EPD's stated validity window (through 2024-04-18) has lapsed as of this update -- check for a renewed version before treating those per-m^2 figures as current. energy_derived_fraction_of_gwp (0.8) derived from Table 16, Annex C, p.77: Electricity (0.56) + Fuels (0.40) of the 1.2 kgCO2e/kg total for float glass -- this applies to raw float glass only; no separate fraction was derived for the processed-glass (m^2) figures, since those come from the AIS EPD rather than IFC's Table 16.

timber._wiring_status: CONNECTED -- classifier.py has a _TIMBER_RE category (CATEGORY_TIMBER) matched against real Ecopolitan BOQ data (75 genuine joinery-item hits, 0 false positives after tightening the regex to require a joinery-product noun after wood(en)); engine.py's compute_line_gwp() has a CATEGORY_TIMBER branch. Real timber lines were found priced 100% in Nos (per-frame/door/window count), not mass or area, so the Nos path (using assumed_mass_kg_per_frame below) is the verified primary path; the kg/MT/m3/m2 paths are unverified fallbacks for BOQs that price timber differently.
timber.not_cea_adjustable: Unlike structural_steel/aluminium/glass/brick_clay above, this factor is NOT eligible for CEA grid adjustment under the current method. It's sourced from ICE v4.1 (UK/EU basis), not IFC India -- IFC's own timber figures were deliberately not used here because they're net-of-carbon-sequestration (negative values) and would need end-of-life modeling this pipeline doesn't have. CEA adjustment requires knowing the factor's assumed baseline grid mix, which is documented for IFC's ~2012 Indian data but not for ICE's UK data -- applying an adjustment without that denominator would mean fabricating a number, same principle already stated in cea_adjustment.py for the ICE concrete fallback table.
timber._assumed_unit_conversions_note: assumed_mass_kg_per_frame (20 kg): typical Indian door/window frame (chowkhat) section ~100mm x 60mm, perimeter ~6.2m for a standard 2.1m x 1m door opening -> volume ~0.037 m3, at a mid-range timber density (~650 kg/m3, between softwood ~500 and hardwood ~800) -> ~24 kg; rounded down slightly to 20 kg to stay conservative for smaller window frames also captured by the same regex. Explicit documented assumption, same pattern as ASSUMED_TILE_SKIRTING_HEIGHT_M in engine.py -- not derived from a real BOQ or source, flag for replacement with actual measured frame sizes if available. assumed_density_kg_per_m3 (650): generic mid-range timber density, consistent with the softwood/hardwood split in excluding_carbon_storage_kgco2e_per_kg below; used only as an unverified fallback for volume-priced timber lines. assumed_areal_mass_kg_per_m2 (8.0 kg/m2): approximates a ~12mm plywood/board panel at ~650 kg/m3 (0.012m x 650 = 7.8, rounded to 8.0); used only as an unverified fallback for area-priced timber lines (e.g. wall paneling).
timber.source: ICE Database v4.1 (Circular Ecology / University of Bath, Oct 2025), Timber sheet, 'excluding carbon storage' section. Cradle-to-gate A1-A3. Deliberately NOT using ICE's 'including carbon storage' figures (which are negative, e.g. generic average -1.03 kgCO2e/kg) or IFC India Table 14's timber lines (also net-of-sequestration, e.g. air-dried sawn timber -1.3, kiln-dried -0.43) -- both require modeling end-of-life to be valid and could produce misleadingly negative totals in a pipeline that doesn't track EOL yet. generic_average (0.49) is the fallback for BOQ lines that just say 'timber'/'wood' without specifying product form; product-specific values should be used when the line item names a form (plywood, MDF, etc.).
